Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Workload targets: we expect sustained 120 RPS with 600 concurrent users during peaks; our SLA target is 500ms P95 and 2s P99. If that changes we'll let you know.
2) Upgrade blackout windows: nightly batch processing runs 01:00-04:00 local (ET) and a weekly reconciliation on Sundays 02:00-06:00. We prefer maintenance outside these windows.
3) Offline ops constraints: our security team requires that any upgrade process be possible while the cluster is air-gapped — i.e., upgrades performed from a secured jump host with signed artifacts; we cannot have outbound access from the inference nodes. Also need documentation for cold-start times after a reboot and KV cache warm-up procedures.

Would be helpful if your hardware spec includes expected cold-start token warm-up times and recommended host-side steps to minimize downtime for model switches. Please also propose 2-3 workshop slots (US Eastern) next week.

Thanks,

Hi Thomas — really helpful, thanks. Answers and actions below: 

1) Hardware & performance notes (attached): the attached redwood-hw-specs.pdf includes an option for 4x A40-class nodes with NVMe-backed model shards for your stated 120 RPS target with P95 ~ 350ms and estimated P99 ~ 1.8s under typical prompt distributions. We included a higher-density 6x-config option if you anticipate burst >150 RPS. The doc also includes an estimated cold-start time for a full node reboot (~90-120s to initial token after model loading) and recommendations to preserve KV cache during rolling restarts (see section 3).

2) Air-gap / offline upgrades: we fully support offline upgrade workflows. Our recommended process:
  - Prepare signed artifacts (container images and model weights) on an approved jump host.
  - Use the onprem-deploy-checklist.xlsx to validate checksums and signatures before importing.
  - Perform rolling restarts node-by-node keeping a minimum quorum (we recommend 3-of-4 up) to preserve serving capacity and KV cache hits.
  - For major model rollouts, stage on a Canary node in an isolated VLAN before full cutover.

3) Maintenance windows: noted — we'll schedule upgrades outside 01:00-04:00 ET and Sunday 02:00-06:00 ET. Please confirm any regional daylight-savings adjustments if relevant.

4) Workshop slots: Dylan can run ops workshop. Proposed slots (US Eastern):
  - Tue 2026-10-06 10:00-11:00 ET
  - Wed 2026-10-07 14:00-15:00 ET
  - Thu 2026-10-08 09:00-10:00 ET

Can you confirm which slot works? I'll prepare a focused agenda covering offline upgrade steps, KV cache strategies, and rollback playbooks.
